title: Conductors and Insulators
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Conductors and Insulators Worksheets (Electricity)
standard_text: Recognise some common conductors and insulators, and associate metals with being good conductors.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on electrical conductors and insulators: metals, plastic, rubber and wood, testing materials in a circuit, and using materials safely. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Test a material in a circuit gap: if the bulb lights, it conducts.
body_html:
How to think about it

Conductors let electricity flow; insulators do not.

  • Metals (copper, steel, aluminium) and graphite are conductors. Plastic, wood, rubber, glass and fabrics are insulators.
  • Test a material by putting it in a gap in a circuit: if the bulb lights, it conducts.
  • Wires have copper inside (conductor) and plastic outside (insulator) to keep us safe.
Example

A steel key in the gap. Bulb?

Steel is a metal conductor

Answer: lights

Example

A rubber band in the gap. Bulb?

Rubber is an insulator

Answer: stays off

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all shiny things conduct.
  • Thinking plastic conducts if it is thin.
  • Using electrical things near water.

faq.q: What is the difference between a conductor and an insulator?
faq.a: A conductor lets electricity flow through it, like copper or steel. An insulator stops electricity flowing, like plastic or rubber.

faq.q: How do you test whether a material conducts?
faq.a: Put it across a gap in a simple circuit with a cell and a bulb. If the bulb lights, the material is a conductor.

faq.q: Why are wires covered in plastic?
faq.a: Plastic is an insulator, so it keeps the electricity inside the copper wire and stops it reaching us.
